$comment: Seeded from the frozen v1 discovery schema at the RFC 0266 §C cut-over (byte-equal to the 2.49.12 derivation); v2-owned since, edited by hand.

subscriptionStates.description: The subscription states the host implements (the §B four-state vocabulary). Absent ⇒ at least `active` + `dead-lettered`.

dedup.description: `true` ⇒ the host de-duplicates inbound events by `dedupKey` within the retention window (§C-1; at-least-once becomes effectively-once).

retryPolicy.description: The host's default delivery retry policy (§C-2).

sources.description: Which trigger sources bridge uniformly. A source listed here MUST have a registerable `TriggerSubscription` driven through the four-state machine AND emit the two `trigger.*` events for that source — the list MUST NOT over-claim a source the host has as a feature but does not wire as a durable trigger subscription. A consumer MUST tolerate any subset.

ingestion.description: RFC 0099 §F.3 (additive). External-event ingestion advertisement — which of `sources[]` the host actually ingests from EXTERNALLY-originated events (`webhook`/`email`/`form`/`stream`/`change`), normalizing each to a `TriggerEvent` (`trigger-event.schema.json`) and starting a run. Absent ⇒ the host does NOT externally-ingest (today's behavior — schedule/queue only). A source in `externalSources[]` MUST actually accept an external event, normalize it, and start a run — over-claiming is a dishonest advertisement. A consumer MUST tolerate any subset.

externalSources.description: Which of `sources[]` are EXTERNALLY ingested per RFC 0099 (`stream`/`change` per RFC 0127). The honesty gate — each MUST normalize to a `TriggerEvent` and start a run.

maxBodyBytes.description: Inbound body cap (webhook body / email / form), reusing the RFC 0076 §B response-cap discipline.

verification.description: Which source-authenticity checks the host performs. An advertised check MUST actually be performed (RFC 0099 §F.3 / UQ1).

inboundSigning.description: RFC 0230. Sender-facing ingest schemes this host implements for `webhook` subscriptions. `standard-webhooks-1`: a sender signs the raw body with the Standard Webhooks headers under the secret returned once at registration; the signature authenticates it (no OpenWOP credential on `ingestUrl`), `webhook-id` is the inbound identity dedup keys on, and the ingest answers 202 delivered / 200 duplicate / 401 signature_invalid / 409 subscription_not_active.

registrationEndpoint.description: `true` ⇒ the host serves `POST /trigger-subscriptions` (RFC 0099 §F.2) for portable external-event subscription creation.

deadLetter.description: RFC 0232 §A (additive). The trigger DELIVERY dead-letter sink, advertised only by a host that serves `GET /trigger-subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/dead-letters` (`listTriggerDeadLetters`). A dead-lettered trigger delivery started no run, so it is on no run's log; this read is where the host's content-free record of it is visible (webhooks.md §Inbound triggers). **Distinct from the top-level `deadLetter` family (RFC 0053), which is the RUN sink**, and from `webhooks.deadLetter` (RFC 0188), which holds OUTBOUND deliveries.

retentionDays.description: How long a dead-lettered delivery stays readable. Observable: a record's `expiresAt − deadLetteredAt` matches it.

maxPageSize.description: The ceiling the host clamps `limit` to.
